home.title: Find the exact pressing.
home.lead: Search by track, pick the artist and album, then compare pressings by country, year and label. Keep a wishlist and a collection of your own.
home.step1Text: No need to remember the album. Type a song and see who pressed it on vinyl.
home.step2Text: Filter by country, year and label to find the one on your shelf, or the one you want.
home.step3Text: A wishlist and a collection, with your own notes and condition grading.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.metaDescription: What Vinilium stores about you, why, who else is involved, and how to delete or export your data.
privacy.lead: Vinilium is a free, non-commercial service. This page says plainly what it stores about you and what you can do about it.
privacy.s1P1: Vinilium is run by a private individual as a free, non-commercial hobby project. The operator appears under the project name or nickname “{operator}” and is based in {country}.
privacy.s1P2: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] How the operator is identified: a private individual shown only under a project name or nickname, with the contact address below. Whether that identification is enough for users in the EU or Norway, and whether anything more (for example a postal address) is required, must be checked. The operator’s legal role for personal data (for example “controller”) and any registration or data-protection contact also belong here.
privacy.s2Intro: Only what the service needs to work:
privacy.s2Account: Your account: your name, your email address and your language. For a password account, the password is stored only in hashed form, which we cannot read. If you sign in with Google, we store the link to your Google account and the name and picture address Google provides. We do not store Google’s access tokens.
privacy.s2Sessions: Your sign-ins: a random session identifier, when it expires, and the IP address and browser description (user agent) of the device you signed in from.
privacy.s2Lists: Your lists: the Discogs release numbers you add, which list each is on (Wishlist or Collection), your own notes and condition grades, and dates.
privacy.s2Counters: Request counters: to protect the service from misuse we count requests per IP address and per account for about a minute at a time.
privacy.s2Emails: Emails: verification and password-reset messages are sent through Brevo, which receives your email address and name for that purpose. Replies to these messages go to our contact address.
privacy.s3P1: No analytics, no advertising, no tracking of what you do on other sites, no payment data. We never ask for your Discogs account or password: record details are fetched by our server with the service’s own Discogs credentials.
privacy.s4P1: Record details (titles, artists, covers, track lists) come from Discogs. Our server asks Discogs for them; your browser does not contact Discogs for them. A short-lived cache (at most 6 hours) holds that data for all users together and contains nothing about you. Links to discogs.com lead to Discogs’ own site, which has its own policies. Vinilium is not affiliated with Discogs.
privacy.s5P1: We use two cookies, both strictly necessary: the sign-in session cookie, and a cookie that remembers your language. There are no analytics or advertising cookies, so there is no cookie banner. If that ever changes, this page and a notice will change first.
privacy.s5P2: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] Whether this cookie approach satisfies the rules that apply in the operator’s country and to the users’ countries.
privacy.s6Intro: Services we use to run Vinilium:
privacy.s6Hosting: Vercel: hosting of the website and its server code.
privacy.s6Database: Neon: the database that holds the data above.
privacy.s6Email: Brevo: sending verification and password-reset emails.
privacy.s6Google: Google: signing in with a Google account, if you choose it.
privacy.s6Discogs: Discogs: the source of record details (see above).
privacy.s6P1: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] Where these providers process data (including outside the EU/EEA), the agreements that cover it, and the wording about them.
privacy.s7P1: Your account and lists stay until you delete your account. Sign-in sessions expire on their own. Request counters last about a minute.
privacy.s7P2: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] Exact retention periods, including how long database backups keep deleted data (this depends on the database plan and is to be filled in by the operator).
privacy.s8Delete: Delete: Account > “Delete my account” removes your account, sessions and lists right away.
privacy.s8Export: Export: Account > “Download my data” gives you your name, email, language and lists as a file; your lists can also be exported as CSV or JSON from the lists page.
privacy.s8Correct: Correct: you can change your language in Account. To change your name or email, use the contact page.
privacy.s8P1: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] A statement of your legal rights (such as access, correction, erasure, portability, objection, and complaint to a supervisory authority) suitable for the operator’s country.
privacy.s9P1: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] Minimum age and wording about children.
privacy.s10P1: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] Passwords are stored hashed, and the site is meant to be used over HTTPS. We take reasonable care, but no system is perfectly secure; the exact wording of this promise must be checked.
privacy.s11P1: If this page changes in a way that matters, the date above changes too.
privacy.s11P2: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] How changes are announced to existing users.
privacy.s2AccountGoogleOnly: Your account: your name, your email address and your language, the link to your Google account, and the name and picture address Google provides. We do not store Google’s access tokens. An account created earlier with a password still holds that password in hashed form, which we cannot read.

terms.lead: Vinilium is a free, non-commercial service. By creating an account you agree to these terms.
terms.s1P1: Vinilium helps you find vinyl pressings and keep a Wishlist and a Collection. It is provided free of charge, as a hobby project, by a private individual shown here as “{operator}” ({country}).

terms.s2A: keep your password private and use the service for yourself, not for resale or commercial purposes;
terms.s2B: do not scrape or automate the service beyond normal use, avoid its rate limits, or try to reach other people’s data or disrupt the service;
terms.s2C: give a real email address that you can read, because we use it to verify your account and reset your password.
terms.s3P1: The notes and condition grades you write are yours. We store and show them to you only to run the service.
terms.s3P2: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] The exact licence you give us for what you write, and any content rules.
terms.s4P1: Record details come from Discogs and stay subject to Discogs’ own terms; you may not copy them out of the service beyond what Discogs allows. Discogs can limit or withdraw access at any time, and then parts of Vinilium that show record details may stop working or show less.
terms.s5P1: The service is free and provided as it is. It can change, pause or stop. We may suspend an account that is used against these terms.
terms.s5P2: [NEEDS LEGAL REVIEW] Warranty disclaimers, the limit of our liability, and what the law allows to be excluded.
